blogs.title: The Border Line: 9th Circuit Upholds Entry Ban but Blocks Defunding of Resettlement
blogs.description: This post analyzes the substantive split in the panel's stay order, distinguishing between the President's broad authority under INA § 1182(f) to suspend refugee admissions and the statutory limitations under the Refugee Act regarding post-admission services. It examines why the court found the government likely to succeed on the entry ban but not on the defunding of cooperative agreements for already admitted refugees.

blogs.title: Textualism in the Refugee Act: Judge Lee's Dissent on Statutory Discretion
blogs.description: A deep dive into the statutory interpretation battle over 8 U.S.C. § 1522. This post explores Circuit Judge Lee's textualist argument that the statute's title ('Authorization') and permissive language grant executive discretion over funding, contrasting with the majority's reading of 'shall' provisions as creating a mandatory duty to provide reception and placement services.

blogs.title: Emergency Stays in Immigration: The 9th Circuit's Evolving Carveouts
blogs.description: Focusing on the procedural history of the case, this post examines the series of stay orders issued between March and September 2025. It highlights the significance of the 'conditionally approved' carveout, which allowed certain refugees to proceed despite the stay, and discusses the implications for emergency litigation strategies in high-stakes immigration enforcement cases.
